questions.question: What is an element?
choices: A substance whose atoms have one proton number
A material separable by filtration into elements

questions.question: What is a compound?
choices: A substance containing elements chemically combined in fixed proportions
A substance containing only one kind of atom

questions.question: What is a mixture?
choices: A substance with one required molecular formula
Two or more substances combined without a fixed chemical composition

questions.question: Which is an example of a homogeneous mixture?
Which is an example of a heterogeneous mixture?
Which formula represents a compound?
What is a solution?
choices: A substance made of only one element
A chemical compound that must be liquid

questions.question: Why is air usually classified as a mixture?
choices: Its gases all have the same chemical formula
It contains only one kind of atom
It contains gases in proportions that can vary
Its components are chemically bonded into one molecule

questions.question: Why is pure water a compound rather than a mixture?
choices: Hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
Every drop contains variable amounts of hydrogen
It can be separated into gases by simple filtering
It is liquid at room temperature

questions.question: How does a mixture's composition differ from a compound's?
choices: A mixture can vary in component proportions; a compound has a fixed composition
A mixture always has one fixed formula
A compound's atom ratio changes with container size

questions.question: Why can filtration separate sand from water?
choices: The filter changes sand into a new compound
The filter breaks water into hydrogen and oxygen
The sand particles are retained while water passes through
The dissolved atoms all become larger

questions.question: Why is filtration alone usually ineffective for removing dissolved salt?
choices: Salt has no mass in solution
Dissolved ions pass through ordinary filter pores with the water
Filtration removes only chemically bonded compounds
Salt becomes part of every water molecule

questions.question: What property allows a magnet to help separate iron filings from sand?
choices: Iron's magnetic response differs from sand's

questions.question: Why does distillation work for suitable liquid mixtures?
choices: Every component has exactly the same boiling point
Components have different vaporization and condensation behavior
The heavier liquid always vanishes first

questions.question: How can a pure element be distinguished conceptually from a compound?
choices: An element must be a gas
A compound contains only one proton number
An element must have a lower mass
An element cannot be chemically decomposed into simpler substances made of different elements

questions.question: A diagram shows only identical O₂ molecules. How should the sample be classified?
A diagram shows identical molecules containing hydrogen and oxygen in the same ratio. What is represented?
A sample contains unbonded copper and sulfur particles. What is it before reaction?
Salt water is heated so that water evaporates and salt remains. What does this demonstrate?
choices: A mixture can be separated using physical differences
Evaporation must convert salt into metal
Water and salt have identical volatility

questions.question: Two clear liquids are compared: pure water and sugar solution. Which conclusion is justified by appearance alone?
choices: Clear appearance does not establish purity
